- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive or neutral (e.g., >0.30), as models tend to overreact to momentum.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or weak (e.g., <0.30), particularly after sharp declines or volatility, indicating model underweighting of bearish signals.
- Correct for lagged mean reversion: if forecast is significantly above or below recent 10-15 day average, adjust downward or upward by 5-10% depending on sentiment direction.
- Reduce forecast magnitude after consecutive high sentiment readings — models often overfit to recent bullish sentiment without accounting for exhaustion.
- When sentiment is volatile or oscillating (e.g., alternating +0.30 and -0.30), reduce forecast confidence and apply smoothing to avoid erratic swings.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid over-optimistic forecasts when recent 18-day history shows consolidation or sideways movement — model should revert to mean rather than extrapolate.
